playbook:
When asked for a hide coordinate, pick a cell that is non-obvious and not the same as my previous round unless I want to telegraph; prefer off-center spots to avoid early clustering (e.g., avoid 5 unless I have a reason).

When the standing order tells me whom to fire on, follow the standing order unless there is a compelling tactical reason not to (e.g., Harbor or an explicit rule change).

When choosing a firing cell, use prior hit/miss information to avoid repeating a known miss against the same target; prefer repeating a cell only if it previously produced a hit on that target or if I intend to brute-force a suspected location.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim that matches the private result exactly (claims must match office info).

Never fire on Harbor (do not target Harbor), unless the rules explicitly allow risking the jettison penalty and I accept the guaranteed heavy penalty to Harbor and myself.

When posting my station note, make a concise routine message that reveals nothing useful about my hidden cell but maintains credibility (e.g., status/ready). Do not include misleading tactical signals that could be used against me.

When offered escort points, only claim an escort if I can arrange or expect mutual naming (i.e., I will name another boat only when I reasonably expect they will name me back that round); otherwise claim none.

When another boat names me as escort, reciprocate that same round if reciprocation is allowed and safe — do it to secure the 5-point mutual escort payoff.

When I have clear evidence (multiple rounds of hit/miss patterns) that a particular opponent is hiding in a specific cell, concentrate fire on that cell when firing at that opponent.

When uncertain about opponents’ hides, vary my fire coordinates to probe the nine cells methodically rather than repeating the same miss-prone coordinates.

When a round’s pattern (my hits/misses and others’ claims) creates contradictions, favor truthful claims and conservative escorts; do not invent hits or fake mutual escorts because claims must match private info and false coordination is brittle.

When learning other boats’ public claims and notes, use them to update likely hide distributions and to decide whether to attempt mutual escort arrangements next round.

If an attempted strategy fails (e.g., repeated misses from a repeated firing coordinate), stop repeating that coordinate and switch to probing; do not persist solely for symmetry.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I choose a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: start near center (4–6) early, then randomize toward edges later if opponents repeatedly find me.

When given a standing-order target, I follow the order unless there is a tactical reason not to (Harbor is the guarded station); otherwise I name the ordered boat as target.

When selecting a firing coordinate, default to mid-board cells (4–6) to maximize hit probability against unknown hides, but shift to a different cluster if an opponent repeatedly hits me from the same side.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I report it exactly (claim truthfully) to avoid contradictions and confusion.

When I receive notes from others, I post neutral, discipline-affirming notes (e.g., “steady on station”) to avoid escalating or revealing unnecessary info.

When the escort stage comes, I default to [salvage: none] unless another boat explicitly names me and mutual naming will occur; only accept escort points if reciprocation is certain.

When someone (including me) threatens Harbor or fires on Harbor, I do not fire on Harbor in retaliation unless seizing the payroll is strategically decisive—Harbor attacks give the shooter +3 and Harbor -3; avoid initiating unless I can absorb the attention.

When an opponent consistently hits me from particular rounds or coordinates, I change my hiding pattern away from predictable central choices and incorporate randomness.

Do not give away extra points by escorting unless I can secure the mutual 5-point exchange; doing nothing is safer than handing opponents points.

If my prior central hides resulted in being frequently hit, stop hiding centrally and diversify; central-first then unpredictable is better than central-only.

When forced to choose between honesty and a deceptive claim that could be disproven by the office or by public records, choose honesty—truthful claims preserve credibility and avoid penalties from contradictions.

2.text:
When choosing a hide, start centrally for balance unless someone is consistently hitting me, in which case move to a different cell away from their likely pattern.

When a round begins and I must post a station note, mirror the group posture ("steady on station") by default; only signal deviation if I'm coordinating an explicit escort or bait plan with a named ally.

When the standing order tells me whom to shoot, target that named live station unless a stronger tactical reason (e.g., to avoid shooting Harbor) is present.

When I pick a firing cell, use recent hit/miss history to predict opponents’ repeat patterns; do not habitually fire the same cell every turn unless that pattern has been rewarded by hits.

Never fire on Harbor unless the tactical reward outweighs the guaranteed heavy penalty; treat Harbor as off-limits by default.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, report that exact result publicly — do not lie or fabricate hits/misses.

When naming an escort, name only actual present boats (no invented names). Do not commit to escorting unless I have a reasonable expectation of reciprocity or when mutual escort will net both of us 5 points.

When another boat names me for escort and I can reciprocate next round, plan to return the claim to secure the mutual reward; when reciprocity is unlikely, do not falsely promise escort.

When I have been targeted repeatedly by the same shooter, change hides and call attention to being under fire in notes only if it helps secure an ally’s reciprocal protection; otherwise move quietly.

When choosing whether to escort or say “none,” prefer “none” over wasting an escort claim on a low-probability or nonreciprocal target.

When coordinating scoring opportunities, use notes to propose explicit mutual escort agreements (name partner and round) so I can act on them reliably in the next stage.
